definitions.explanation: A tall, pointed tower on a building, especially a church or mosque. Also used for any tall, tapering architectural structure.

examples.japanese: {教会|きょうかい}の{尖塔|せんとう}が{空|そら}に{伸|の}びている。
examples.english: The church spire stretches toward the sky.

examples.japanese: {遠|とお}くから{尖塔|せんとう}の{先端|せんたん}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: I could see the tip of the steeple from far away.

examples.japanese: ゴシック{建築|けんちく}の{大聖堂|だいせいどう}は、{高|たか}い{尖塔|せんとう}が{特徴|とくちょう}だ。
examples.english: Gothic cathedrals are characterized by their tall spires.

notes:
USAGE:
Used in architecture, travel writing, and descriptions of Western buildings. A compound of {尖|せん} (pointed) and {塔|とう} (tower).

NOTE: This is a homophone of {先頭|せんとう} (the lead, the front), {戦闘|せんとう} (battle), and {銭湯|せんとう} (public bath).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {教会|きょうかい}の{尖塔|せんとう} (church steeple)
- {尖塔|せんとう}がそびえる (a spire towers up)
- ゴシック{様式|ようしき}の{尖塔|せんとう} (Gothic-style spire)
